subject: Request: snapshot of active subprocessors + ephemeral key onboarding evidence
messages:
From: Emily Harper <e.harper@lakesidehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lakeside Health Security Team <security@lakesidehealth.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Info request — active subprocessors + temporary access controls

Hi Ben,

Thanks for helping us with the SOC 2 intake. The procurement team needs a short, machine-friendly snapshot of all active subprocessors that have had temporary (ephemeral) API keys or privileged access in the last 12 months. Specifically: a CSV with vendor name, start/end of access, scope (read/write), and whether onboarding checklist and signed NDA are present.

Also: can you include a short statement or the policy that governs ephemeral key issuance and rotation for subprocessors (we need the version in effect on 2026-12-31)? If you have a PDF or signed attestation, that would be ideal.

We'd like the materials by EOD Tuesday (US PST). Happy to extend if you need more time.

Best,
Emily Harper
Sr. Information Risk Analyst
Lakeside Health

[Attachment requested: example CSV template]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Harper <e.harper@lakesidehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Info request — active subprocessors + temporary access controls

Hi Emily — thanks for the heads up. We're on it. Quick clarifying Qs before we package:

- Do you want vendors that only used console-based service accounts (no API keys) included?
- For "scope", should we standardize to the terms: admin / read-write / read-only / limited-svc?

Marissa: can you pull the subprocessor snapshot export and check the ephemeral-key audit logs for 2026?
Sean: linking the signed onboarding checklist for the larger vendors (I have PDFs for three).

If that's OK, we'll aim to deliver the CSV plus the rotation policy PDF and the signed checklists by end of tomorrow. If Lakeside needs a signed attestation, we can provide a short one from Security.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T15:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Info request — active subprocessors + temporary access controls

On Mon, Jan 10, 2027 at 11:05 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa: can you pull the subprocessor snapshot export and check the ephemeral-key audit logs for 2026?
> Sean: linking the signed onboarding checklist for the larger vendors (I have PDFs for three).

Done — I exported the snapshot and cross-checked the audit logs. Notes:

- We've included console-only service accounts in a separate column (include_console_accounts = true) but filtered them into their own rows so Lakeside can ignore them if desired.
- Standardized scope to: admin / read-write / read-only / svc-limited.
- The rotation policy PDF attached is versioned (v1.3) and was in effect 2026-07-01 through 2026-12-31. It documents 7-day ephemeral tokens for vendors that require programmatic access and automatic rotation with short TTLs.
- I attached three onboarding-checklist-signed PDFs for SecureProc, NimbusOps, and CloudLatch. The CSV references each filename.

Attaching: subprocessor_snapshot.csv, ephemeral_key_rotation_policy.pdf, onboarding-checklist-signed.pdf

Marissa Cole
Vendor Risk Analyst
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Harper <e.harper@lakesidehealth.com>
Cc: Lakeside Health Security Team <security@lakesidehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T15:44:00-08:00
Subject: Final delivery — subprocessor snapshot + policy (with attachments)

Emily — attaching the snapshot and supporting docs as requested. Quick summary for your intake team:

- subprocessor_snapshot.csv: 27 entries covering all active subprocessors in the last 12 months. Columns: vendor_name, vendor_domain, access_start, access_end, access_type (api_key / console / service_account), scope (admin / read-write / read-only / svc-limited), onboarding_checklist (filename or NONE), nda_signed (yes/no), notes.
- ephemeral_key_rotation_policy.pdf (v1.3): describes issuance, TTL (7 days for ephemeral API keys), automatic rotation, audit logging, and emergency revocation processes.
- onboarding-checklist-signed.pdf: consolidated signed checklist package for the three vendors mentioned earlier.

If Lakeside needs a short signed attestation that the CSV was generated from our audited logs and matches the rotation policy in effect on 2026-12-31, we can have Security sign and return it — just confirm the signer and whether an electronic signature is acceptable.

Thanks for the patience. Ping me if you want a live walk-through of any vendor rows.

Best,
Ben

[Attachment stubs: subprocessor_snapshot.csv (CSV, 27 rows), ephemeral_key_rotation_policy.pdf (PDF, 12 pages), onboarding-checklist-signed.pdf (PDF, 6 pages)]
